validity.recommendation: No existence/classification/duplicate/attribution defect found; row is well-sourced and correctly classified. See separate spec concern on Capacity (current vs. design figure).
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed by independent primary sources of different types -- a federal statistical database (EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects historical workbook, which carries a discrete 'Bison Pipeline Project' row with operator 'Bison Pipeline LLC', FERC docket CP09-161, in-service 2011-01-14), the operator's current asset page (tcenergy.com/operations/natural-gas/bison-pipeline/), two independent news organizations covering the pipeline's July 2011 rupture (Casper Star-Tribune via journalstar.com, and a CBC News investigation dated Oct 2012), and two SEC EDGAR filings (TC PipeLines LP 10-K Exhibit 21.1 naming 'Bison Pipeline LLC' as a wholly-owned subsidiary, and the Mar 3 2021 8-K merger press release). This is not a GEM-only entity -- it has a public FERC docket, a federal EIA project record, and sustained press coverage independent of GEM. CLASSIFICATION: correctly classified as an operating interstate natural gas transmission pipeline (FERC-jurisdictional, EIA Pipeline Type='Interstate', Fuel=Gas) -- no evidence it is a gathering/process line. DUPLICATE: checked against the roster's Williston/Bakken cluster (P0281 Williston Basin, P2099 Northern Border, P0367 Valley Expansion, P3158 Traill County, P0306 Doosan Bobcat, P0316 South Saskatchewan Access) -- Bison is a distinct FERC pipeline (docket CP09-161) that DELIVERS INTO Northern Border Pipeline (P2099) at its North Dakota terminus per every source read; that interconnect explains why sources discuss the two together and is not evidence of a duplicate/relabel. No relabel candidate found. Of the row's 9 harvested wiki citations, all 9 were opened/attempted: the bit.ly shortener (cite_note-source1-1) resolves to bisonpipelinellc.com, which no longer resolves in DNS at all (confirmed dead, not merely blocked); the tcpipelineslp.com/assets/bison/ URL (cite_note-3) 301-redirects to the generic TC Energy homepage with zero mentions of 'Bison' (dead as a Bison-specific page, superseded below by the live tcenergy.com asset page found independently); the EIA 'Natural Gas Data' landing page (data.php, cite_note-eia) is a navigation surface that never names Bison itself, so it fails the naming/relevance rule as cited -- I instead used the specific EIA workbook the site links out to (EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects.xlsx), which explicitly contains a 'Bison Pipeline Project' row and is a materially better source than the harvested landing page; the Pipeline & Gas Journal 2011 article (cite_note-PGJ) 404s and has no Wayback capture (archive.org's availability API was rate-limited (429) throughout this session -- a later retry is worth trying); the Reuters 2008 acquisition story (cite_note-5) 401s live and its Wayback capture is a JS-rendered SPA shell with no readable article text; nrdc.org (cite_note-8) 403s and is a Keystone-XL opinion piece only tangentially referencing Bison, not pursued further given the strong existence pool already assembled; btuanalytics.com (cite_note-BTU-9) has been retired entirely (redirects to a generic FactSet marketing page, zero Bison content). Only journalstar.com (cite_note-6) and cbc.ca (cite_note-CBC-7) were live and content-bearing among the harvested pool; both required a manual ROT47 decode of Lee Enterprises' obfuscated paywall-protected article body (visible in page source as 'kAm...k^Am' segments) to read the actual prose -- this decode surfaced the 30-inch diameter, 303-mile length, 477 MMcf/d design capacity, and August 2010 construction start that are staged below. Two additional sources beyond the harvested pool were found via targeted search: the live TC Energy asset page (not in the wiki's citation list at all) and two SEC EDGAR filings (also not harvested) that settle the Operator/Owner questions.

validity.recommendation: Verify Bison's current firm/operational capacity (e.g. via TC Energy's informational postings at ebb.tceconnects.com/infopost/, or a recent FERC Form 2) and update Capacity if a precise current figure is found; GEM's 477 MMcf/d is the 2011 as-built design figure, not necessarily today's operating capacity.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's Capacity=477.00 MMcf/d matches the pipeline's ORIGINAL 2011 design capacity exactly as stated by two independent sources at the time of construction: the EIA historical-projects workbook ('Additional Capacity (MMcf/d)' = 477 on the Bison Pipeline Project row) and the Casper Star-Tribune's July 25 2011 rupture story, which states 'The 303-mile line was designed to transport up to 477 million cubic feet a day of natural gas... The pipeline is rated to handle up to a billion cubic feet' (the latter figure appears to be a garbled/overstated quote elsewhere in the same article and should not be used). However, TC Energy's OWN current (2026) asset page for Bison states: 'the pipeline has the ability to offer almost 420 million cubic feet per day (MMcf/d) of operational capacity' -- a present-day figure roughly 12% below the 2011 design capacity GEM carries. This is exactly the kind of stale-spec pattern this batch is calibrated to expect: a value that was correct in 2011 and has not been revisited since. I could not pin down an exact current number ('almost 420' is the operator's own imprecise phrasing) so I am not proposing a replacement value -- only flagging that the CURRENT figure likely differs materially from the value on an 'operating' row, and naming where to look for a precise number (TC Energy's shipper info-posting portal, which requires an account, or a recent FERC Form 2 filing for Bison Pipeline LLC, neither of which I could access in this pass).

TC PipeLines LP was itself a separately publicly-traded partnership (NYSE: TCP) until TC Energy completed a merger acquiring all remaining public units on March 3, 2021 (per TC PipeLines LP's own 8-K press release that day, 'TCP becoming an indirect, wholly owned subsidiary of TC Energy') -- so GEM's current Owner1='TC Energy [100%]' is consistent with the POST-merger ownership chain (TC Energy -> wholly-owned TC PipeLines LP -> wholly-owned Bison Pipeline LLC). I am citing only the 10-K exhibit as the proposed ref because it is the one document that actually NAMES Bison Pipeline LLC; the March 2021 merger press release is a real and directly relevant supporting fact but does not itself name Bison, so per the naming/relevance rule I am not listing it as a verified ref -- it is cited here in prose only as the chain-completing fact a reviewer can check independently (SEC EDGAR, TC PipeLines LP CIK 0001075607, 8-K filed 2021-03-03, accession 0001104659-21-031578).
